newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown has helped strengthen sterling-Lilley.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown has helped strengthen sterling-Lilley.

text.p: Conservative treasury spokesman Peter Lilley on Tuesday accused Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown of adding to the strength of sterling by talking of a consumer boom and then failing to act to control it.
"Gordon Brown is not the only influence on the markets," Lilley told journalists during a briefing on the finance bill which implements Brown's recent budget.
"But his words unmatched by actions did exacerbate tendencies in that direction (of higher sterling)."

Lilley had been asked whether he agreed with remarks made earlier on Tuesday by German finance minister Theo Waigel that the strength of sterling and the dollar against the mark was an over-reaction by the foreign exchange markets.

Lilley criticised Brown for having insisted that there was a boom in consumer spending and then taking few measures in the budget to curb it. Brown's major tax-raising moves were directed at the corporate sector and at pension funds.
This had resulted in the "worst of all possible worlds", he said.
Lilley said Brown's move to give the Bank of England freedom over interest rates had resulted in rates now being 3/4 point higher than at the May 1 election.
This, together with cuts in mortgage interest tax relief announced in the budget, had left a family with an average mortgage 30 stg a month worse off.
Lilley said that in debate on the bill in parliament later on Tuesday the Conservatives would press Brown to delay the tax relief cuts until rates had returned to pre-election levels.

He said families would also eventually face extra payments for services such as gas, water and electricity of about 30 pounds a month because of Brown's windfall tax on "excess" profits made by privatised utilities. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
